cleanIntro: The Drake is one of four over-under models CZ's shotgun book names by designation, and it strips to three pieces the way every break gun does: forestock off, barrels off the hinge pin, receiver in your hand. The book is organised by ACTION TYPE rather than by model, so only the over-under paragraphs describe your gun — the self-loading and pump-action passages on the same pages belong to the CZ 1012 and the CZ 612 and describe mechanisms a Drake does not have. Everything below is read off the English section of CZ's SHOTGUNS manual, PDF pages 2 to 14.

steps.title: The Drake is an over-under — only the over-under paragraphs apply
steps.action: Before following any procedure in this book, place your gun in CZ's own list. The over-under range is Supreme Field, Redhead Premier, Drake and All American; the CZ 1012 is the self-loading model and the CZ 612 the pump-action. Use only the sentences written for the over-under.
steps.prose: This one book carries three completely different mechanisms in the same numbered sections, and the paragraphs sit directly next to one another on the page. A Drake has no bolt release, no magazine tube in the forestock and no magazine closure to unscrew — those all belong to the 1012 and the 612. Reading a self-loading instruction onto a break gun sends you looking for controls that do not exist and, worse, teaches a clearing method that does not clear your gun.
steps.quote: The over-under shotgun product range includes the models Supreme Field, Redhead Premier, Drake and All American.
steps.cite: CZ SHOTGUNS — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Terminology and Description, p.5

steps.title: There is no automatic safety on this gun
steps.action: Do not assume the safety reapplies when you break the gun open. CZ states in capitals that the firearm is not equipped with automatic safety. On an over-under the safety is a manual slide: back to secure, forward in the direction of fire to unlock, and it can be pushed back to safe at any time.
steps.prose: Many break-action shotguns re-engage the safety every time the top lever is worked, and shooters carry that expectation across from gun to gun. A Drake does not do it, so a gun that was fired, opened, reloaded and closed is a gun with the safety wherever you last put it. CZ's own instruction is that the safety should be unlocked only immediately before firing, once the gun is already pointed somewhere safe. On an over-under the safety may also carry the firing order selector inside it, so check that you are moving the safety and not the selector.
steps.quote: THE FIREARM IS NOT EQUIPPED WITH AUTOMATIC SAFETY.
steps.cite: CZ SHOTGUNS — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Instructions for Use — CAUTION following Loading the firearm, p.7

steps.title: Break it open and clear both chambers
steps.action: Push the top lever fully to the right with the thumb of your right hand and at the same time push the barrels fully down with your left hand. Look into BOTH chambers and account for whatever comes out.
steps.prose: What happens next depends on how your Drake is fitted. If it has ejectors, fired cases are thrown clear — so make sure there is space and remember they are hot; a round that MISFIRED is only partially extracted, which is CZ's way of keeping a live shell in your hand instead of in the air. If it has extractors instead, both shells are only lifted proud for you to pull out by hand. Either way, look down both tubes rather than trusting the throw, because a partially extracted shell looks very much like an ejected one from above.
steps.quote: When opening the shotgun barrel bundle, make sure there is enough free space for ejecting hot cartridge cases. If a round has misfired, the ejector will just partially extract it to facilitate its removal.
steps.cite: CZ SHOTGUNS — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Instructions for Use — Loading the firearm, p.7
steps.warn: THE FIREARM IS LOCKED PROPERLY IF THE TOP LEVER IS PERPENDICULAR TO THE FACE OF THE BARREL BUNDLE! CZ states that if it is not perpendicular, and/or there is a clearance between the face of the barrels and the receiver, the Drake may fire when the safety is off and the trigger is pressed — and that such handling is PROHIBITED. Check the lever every time you close the gun, not just after a strip.

steps.title: Chokes stay put unless the gun is unloaded and safe
steps.action: If the session includes changing or cleaning the chokes, do it only with the shotgun unloaded and its handling completely safe. Chokes are marked on the muzzle with the same designation given in CZ's table, so read the mark rather than counting notches from memory.
steps.prose: This is the one operation on a Drake that puts your hand at the muzzle, which is why CZ gives it its own capitalised caution. The steel-shot column of the table is the part worth reading twice: the 4/4 Full choke is listed as NOT RECOMMENDED for steel shot at all, and every other tube shifts one step more open when steel is used instead of lead. A choke wound in dirty seizes, so clean the threads and the tube seat while the barrels are off rather than forcing a stuck tube later.
steps.quote: Never perform any operations on the choke unless the firearm is unloaded and its handling is completely safe!
steps.cite: CZ SHOTGUNS — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Instructions for Use — Set of replaceable chokes, CAUTION, p.10

steps.title: Forestock latch out, forestock off the barrels
steps.action: With the firearm LOCKED — that is, closed — tilt out the forestock latch while pressing the forestock lightly towards the barrel. Then take the forestock off the barrels.
steps.prose: The order is not negotiable on a break gun: the forestock comes off with the action closed, because a forestock removed from an open gun takes the ejector work with it and can spring the ejector hammers. The light inward pressure is what unloads the latch so it will tilt — pull the latch cold against a forestock that is not pressed in and you bend it. Set the forestock down on its side; the ejector rods and any cocking parts inside it are the reason it is not just a piece of wood.
steps.quote: In the case of the over-under shotgun, with the firearm locked, tilt out the forestock latch (Fig. 8) while lightly pressing the forestock towards the barrel. Remove the forestock from the barrels.
steps.cite: CZ SHOTGUNS — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Disassembly after cleaning, p.11

steps.title: Rotate the barrels about 40 degrees and lift them off the pin
steps.action: Take the receiver in your right hand and the barrels in your left. Press the top lever to unlock the bolt and rotate the barrels around the hinge pin. At roughly 40 degrees of rotation the barrels will slide off the pin.
steps.prose: Forty degrees is well past the normal open position, so the barrels come off at a point you never reach while shooting — which is exactly why a Drake does not shed its barrels in the field. Hold the receiver, not the stock, and let the barrels come to you; dropping a barrel bundle on its muzzles is how a rib gets sprung. Keep the hinge pin and its bearing surfaces clean and lightly oiled, because that pin and the locking bolt are the two wearing surfaces that decide whether the gun stays tight.
steps.quote: Press on the handle to unlock the bolt and rotate the barrels around the pin. When the barrels have been turned by approximately 40°, they can be slid out of the pin.
steps.cite: CZ SHOTGUNS — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Disassembly after cleaning, p.11

steps.title: Field strip complete — and this is the boundary
steps.action: Barrels, forestock and receiver with stock: three pieces and nothing else. Do not remove any other parts; if you believe the shotgun needs adjustment or repair, that work goes to a specialized workshop.
steps.prose: Those three pieces reach everything the cleaning section asks for: both bores and both chambers from the breech end, the barrel flats and the extractor or ejector faces, the standing breech and the water table on the receiver, and the hinge pin and locking bolt. Everything past that on a Drake is the ejector mechanism and the trigger plate, both spring-loaded assemblies that CZ does not open for the owner in this book. The caution below the reassembly paragraph is the whole boundary in one sentence.
steps.quote: CAUTION: Do not remove any other parts. If you believe the firearm requires an adjustment or repair, entrust this work to a specialized workshop!
steps.cite: CZ SHOTGUNS — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Reassembling, CAUTION, p.11

deepAbsentReason: CZ's SHOTGUNS manual publishes no procedure past the three-piece break-gun strip for any over-under, the Drake included. The disassembly paragraph ends with the barrels sliding off the hinge pin, and the reassembly paragraph is followed immediately by "CAUTION: Do not remove any other parts. If you believe the firearm requires an adjustment or repair, entrust this work to a specialized workshop!" (p.11). Nothing about the ejector mechanism, the trigger plate, the top lever or the locking bolt is documented as owner work, and the book gives no second-level procedure for the over-under at all. The two further disassembly paragraphs on that same page belong to the CZ 1012 self-loading and CZ 612 pump-action models — different mechanisms with magazine closures and bolt assemblies that a Drake does not have — and applying them here would be substitution, not a deep clean.

cleaning.name: BORES & CHAMBERS
tasks: With no or few shots fired, run a dry cloth on the cleaning rod through each bore and chamber, changing cloths, until the last swab comes out clean — both barrels, top and bottom
For heavy fouling, brush cleaning agent into the bore and chamber, let it work about 10 minutes, then brush them out
Rod and brush enter from the CHAMBER end so the muzzle and the choke threads are never used as a guide; run the brush the full length of the bore before reversing, or it jams
Wipe both bores and chambers dry with clean cloth and check that all the combustion products have been removed
Take the chokes out, clean the tubes and the threads in the muzzle, and check that the seat is clean before they go back — only ever with the gun unloaded and safe

cleaning.name: BARREL FLATS, RECEIVER & HINGE
tasks: Clean the barrel flats, the lumps and the extractor or ejector faces with a dry cloth, an old toothbrush, a brass brush or a wooden scraper
Clean the standing breech, the water table and the locking bolt recesses in the receiver — that is where a break gun's fouling actually collects
Wipe and lightly oil the hinge pin and its bearing surfaces; that pin and the locking bolt are the two surfaces that decide whether the gun stays tight
Never use the bore cleaning solution on these components — it stays between parts and causes corrosion after longer exposure
Make sure no cloth lint or brush bristles are left anywhere on the gun

cleaning.name: STOCK, FORESTOCK & PRESERVATION
tasks: Maintain the stock with a dry cloth or a wooden furniture polishing agent — CZ's own instruction for the woodwork
Set the forestock down on its side and clean it without disturbing the ejector rods inside it
Once cleaned, wipe bores, chambers and all accessible parts dry and rub them with a cloth soaked in preservative oil or use a preservative oil spray, then wipe off any excess
Wipe the bores dry before shooting

At low temperatures remove the oil from all accessible parts or use a lubricant designed for that environment; keep thick grease for long-term storage in harsh conditions only, and remove it completely before use

reassembly: Turn the bolt handle up to the end stop of its open position first — the barrels cannot be inserted into the receiver while the handle is not arrested.
Insert the barrels into the receiver, slide them onto the hinge pin and rotate them closed.
Set the forestock on the front surface of the receiver and rotate it along the receiver guiding surfaces to press it to the barrel; the latch will engage the forestock hook.
Break the gun and close it again to check the assembly is correct — CZ advises this as the confirmation step.
Wipe the bores dry before the shotgun is fired.
fncheck: Both chambers confirmed empty. Close the gun and look at the top lever: it must be PERPENDICULAR to the face of the barrel bundle, because CZ states the firearm is only locked properly in that position and that a lever off perpendicular, or any clearance between the barrel faces and the receiver, means the gun may fire when the safety is off and the trigger is pressed — handling it in that state is prohibited. Then check the safety slides back to expose the "S" and blocks the trigger, remembering there is no automatic safety on this gun so it stays wherever you leave it. If the barrel selector is fitted, confirm it moves right for the bottom barrel first and left for the top. Finally break and close the gun once more and confirm the forestock latch is fully engaged on its hook.
